overview: Global (2026) roadmap for entry → senior level Android developers. Covers Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP), declarative UI (Compose), on-device AI (Gemini Nano), and multi-device optimization.

steps.title: 1. Modern Kotlin & Multitasking
steps.description: Kotlin is the non-negotiable standard. In 2026, proficiency means mastering asynchronous and multi-platform syntax.
subtopics: Kotlin Foundations: Null safety, data classes, and sealed types
Advanced Coroutines: Structured concurrency, Scopes, and Flows for reactive state
Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP): Sharing business logic between Android, iOS, and Web
Kotlinx Serialization: The KMP-first alternative to Moshi/GSON

steps.title: 2. Declarative UI & Adaptive Layouts
steps.description: Jetpack Compose is the primary UI framework. XML is now largely for legacy maintenance.
subtopics: Jetpack Compose: State-driven UI, Recomposition, and Modifiers
Navigation 3.0: Composable-to-Composable navigation (goodbye NavController)
Adaptive Design: Building for foldables, tablets, and large screens
Material Design 3 (M3): Dynamic theming and accessible design components
Graphics & Animation: Compose-native canvas and micro-interactions

steps.title: 3. On-Device AI & Intelligence
steps.description: 2026 is the year of 'AI-Native' apps. AI is now a foundation, not a feature.
subtopics: Gemini Nano & AICore: Running LLMs directly on the device for privacy
TensorFlow Lite: Deploying custom ML models for image/speech recognition
MediaPipe: High-level vision and gesture tasks
Vector Search: Using on-device vector stores (e.g., MongoDB Atlas) for AI retrieval
Prompt Engineering: Crafting local prompts for text summarization and smart replies

steps.title: 4. Architecture & Data Flow
steps.description: Scaling apps with clean, testable, and maintainable patterns.
subtopics: MVVM & MVI: Choosing between state-driven and intent-driven architectures
Dependency Injection: Hilt (Standard) vs. Koin (KMP Favorite)
Persistence: Room (SQLite) vs. DataStore for key-value pairs
Networking: Retrofit for REST vs. Ktor for KMP-compatible requests
Offline-First: Syncing data with WorkManager and repository patterns

steps.title: 5. Security, Privacy & Performance
steps.description: Handling stricter OS permissions and optimizing for battery/data.
subtopics: Privacy-by-Design: Local data processing and strict permission handling
Security Models: Zero-trust, biometrics, and end-to-end encryption
Performance Profiling: Using Android Studio Profiler to monitor CPU and battery
Baseline Profiles: Reducing app startup time and jank

steps.title: Capstone Projects: 2026 Portfolio Ideas
steps.description: Projects that prove you can handle modern device constraints and AI.

projects.name: KMP Fitness Tracker
projects.description: A fitness app sharing logic between Android and iOS. Uses Health Connect API and KMP business logic.

projects.name: Privacy-First AI Life Manager
projects.description: An agentic personal assistant using Gemini Nano for local text summarization of notes and emails.

projects.name: Adaptive Foldable E-Commerce
projects.description: A shopping app that changes layout dynamically when folded/unfolded, with multi-window support.
